body:
Fixes #2408

## What happened

The `/claude https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196 --think high` task ran for about 17 hours and hit two out-of-memory events:

- **22:47.** `npm run check` was OOM-killed (exit 137). Claude **survived** and carried on. Docker set the container-wide `State.OOMKilled` flag, which stays set until the container exits.
- **07:08.** solve stopped **on purpose** ("Auto-restart limit reached after 5 iterations"), and the container exited 1. Because the sticky flag was still set, the bot read this as an OOM casualty. It spent its whole recovery budget (1/1) on a fresh launch with a new execution id, and the log was split.
- **07:11.** Three overlapping monitor ticks completed the old session three times. The last one overwrote "recovering" with **"❌ Work session failed (exit code: 1)"**, while `/queue` showed the recovery as processing for 5h 31m.
- **13:37.** Two Claude subagents ran `cargo test` in separate worktrees, and the kernel SIGKILLed Claude (exit 137). solve stopped and posted two failure reports, and the container exited 1. Six overlapping monitor ticks then posted six logs and six notices. One of them contained `[object Object]`.

The timeline, evidence (sanitized log excerpts, PR comment data, the issue screenshots) and research are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md).

## Root causes and fixes

| #   | Problem | Fix | Test (`tests/issue-2408-oom-recovery-reporting.test.mjs`) |
| --- | ------- | --- | ---- |
| RC1 | The 30 s `setInterval` monitor overlapped itself while a completion uploaded a 100 MB log, so one exit was completed 3× and 6×. Later copies found the budget spent and reported ❌ | `sessionsInFlight` per-session guard in `monitorSessions`; `already-recovered` latch in `recoverKilledSession` | "overlapping monitor ticks recover a killed session once and report it once", "a repeated completion for an already-recovered session does not start another one" |
| RC2 | Exit 1 + sticky `OOMKilled` read before the log footer was classified as "killed: out of memory" | Only exit 137 (or no exit code) with a dead backend is a kill; exit 1–127 is an OOM *event* during a failed session | "an exit 1 with the OOM flag and no footer yet is a survived OOM event, not a kill" |
| RC3 | A deliberate solve stop after a survived OOM event spent the recovery budget | New `session-kill-attribution.lib.mjs` scans the log tail for solve's own stop markers (auto-restart, auto-resume or usage limit). The exit is reported, not recovered | "a deliberate solve stop after an OOM event is reported, not recovered" |
| RC4 | A budget of 1 cannot cover a second OOM in a long run | `--session-kill-resume-attempts` defaults to 3 (docs in 4 languages) | "a second OOM in a long run can still be recovered by default" |
| RC5 | A SIGKILLed AI tool (exit 137) ended the whole `--auto-restart-until-mergeable` / watch run | New `solve.tool-kill-resume.lib.mjs` posts "⚠️ Working process killed (exit code 137, likely out of memory)" and resumes the **same** session in the same container and log. The feedback asks Claude to run builds one at a time. It shares the budget above | "a tool process killed by SIGKILL resumes its own session in-process, with a warning" |
| RC6 | Kill notice printed `[object Object]` as the manual resume command | Render `command.display` | "the pull-request notice renders a resume command object, never \"[object Object]\"" |
| RC7 | Task message and `/queue` showed only the recovery session's time, with no notion of "recovered" | `rootStartTime` + recovery count. The headline is ⚠️ "Work session finished successfully after automatic recovery (automatic recoveries: N)". `/queue` shows the total time and `🔁 N` (new `recovered`/`recoveries` keys in en/ru/hi/zh) | "the headline says how many automatic recoveries the work needed", "the queue shows the total active time of recovered work and its recovery count" |
| RC8 | Log split across execution ids: a resource-limited session cannot use start-command's same-container resume, because `docker commit` + `docker run` drops the limits | On start-command ≥ 0.35.0 (start#176, now pinned) a resource-limited session **resumes in place** under the same id and log. The `$` version gates it, CPU/RAM are re-asserted with `docker update`, and the writable-layer usage so far is carried into the disk allowance (`containerFilesystemInheritedBytes`). With an older `$`, the message names the earlier logs, for example `🆔 Execution: 88951cec (earlier logs: 0760afb4)` (`previousExecutionUuids` is persisted). Upstream: link-foundation/start#176 | "a fresh recovery launch keeps pointing at the earlier execution logs"; `tests/test-issue-2408-limited-in-place-resume.mjs` |
| RC9 | "…backend is still alive" verbose line printed on every poll (10,047 lines in one bot log) | Printed once per session | "the still-alive OOM verbose line is printed once, not on every poll" |
| RC10 | Two failure reports from one solve run (5953703216 + 5953753740) | Already fixed in v2.33.5 (#2397); the incident ran on 2.33.2 | "the exit notifier does not post a second failure report after the loop posted one" |

The citation for the sticky `State.OOMKilled` semantics now points at moby's `daemon/monitor.go` (`EventOOM`) and `daemon/container/state.go` (`SetRunning`).

## Follow-up: the 2026-10-03 rerun (PR comment)

The rerun of the same task (solve v2.33.7, bot still on pre-PR code) repeated RC3 and RC1 between [5965062164](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965062164) and [5965532446](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965532446). solve stopped on purpose ("❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached", exit 1), but an OOM event at 16:55 the day before had left the sticky `OOMKilled` flag set. The bot therefore started recovery session `9187bb95`, which runs `solve` again with a fresh auto-restart budget: this is why it "continued to work in the background". Three more overlapping ticks posted three more log + notice pairs, and the last one set Telegram to ❌.

- **Regression test** on the real log tail (`docs/case-studies/issue-2408/logs/solve-log-7edfe0cf-auto-restart-limit-tail.txt`): four concurrent ticks → no launch, one notice, one Telegram completion, and one `session_kill_recovery_decision` event with `deliberateStop=auto-restart-limit`, `attemptRecovery=false`.
- **Every restart path audited** (solve auto-restart, auto-resume, in-process tool-kill resume, bot kill/OOM recovery, start-command `--on-kill-resume`); the triggers and bounds are in the [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md#audit-of-every-restart-path).
- **Gaps found by the audit and fixed**, each with a test in `tests/issue-2408-restart-paths.test.mjs` that fails before the fix:
  - B1: a session SIGKILLed *after* solve printed "❌ Auto-restart limit reached" was still recovered. The deliberate-stop check now covers killed sessions too.
  - B2: exit 0 + sticky flag + no footer yet was turned into "oom-killed" (137). A terminal exit 0 now stays a success.
  - B3: "No progress between sessions" / "identical results" and "SUBSCRIPTION/ACCESS UNAVAILABLE" are now deliberate stops. "AI session failed" stays recoverable (#2301).
  - B4: `/stop <root id>`, the id the chat shows, did not reach the recovery session, so a user stop was followed by another automatic recovery. It now matches `executionUuid`, `rootSessionName` and `killRecoveryOfSession`.
  - B5: a resumed solve child killed by a signal made the auto-continue parent `process.exit(null)`, i.e. **0**. It now exits 128 + n (SIGKILL → 137) and logs the signal.
  - B7: stop markers matched anywhere in a line, including quoted tool output. They are now anchored to the start of a log line.
- **Logging:** `session_kill_recovery_decision` (exit code, status, killed, oomEventOnly, deliberateStop, diskLimitExceeded, attemptRecovery) for every kill/OOM exit; `session_kill_not_recovered` with the reason; `[VERBOSE]` lines for the skipped recovery and for the `$` version gate.
- **Upstream:** start-command 0.35.0's new `--on-kill-resume` has the same sticky-flag bug, one layer down (`isKilledExit(1, "true") === true`), so it is not used. Filed as [link-foundation/start#178](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/178) with a repro and fix.
- **Dependencies:** start-command 0.35.0 (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dind, Dockerfile.e2e), eslint 10.12.0 and secretlint 13.0.7. `npm outdated` is now empty, `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.11 is the latest, and every GitHub Action is at its latest release.

## Answers to the questions in the issue

- **Does `0760afb4` contain the full 15 hours?** No. It covers 20:38:25 → 07:09:43 (10h 31m). The recovery ran as a fresh launch with execution `88951cec` and its own log. With start-command ≥ 0.35.0 (pinned here) a resource-limited recovery now stays in the same id and log. With an older `$`, the Telegram message names both ids.
- **The "crazy comments" after 5953703216:** see [The thirteen comments](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md#the-thirteen-comments-after-5953703216). Each one maps to RC1–RC6 or RC10.
- **start-command initial + recovery command:** filed as [link-foundation/start#176](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/176), with a repro, workaround and suggested fix. The repro is `experiments/issue-2408-docker-commit-drops-limits.sh`: the original container has `Memory=268435456 … PidsLimit=64`, and the resumed one has `Memory=0 … PidsLimit=<no value>`.

## How to reproduce / verify

```bash
node tests/issue-2408-oom-recovery-reporting.test.mjs   # 13/13 pass
node tests/test-issue-2408-limited-in-place-resume.mjs  # 27/27 pass
node --test tests/issue-2408-restart-paths.test.mjs     # 5/5 pass (all 5 fail on the code before the fix)
node experiments/issue-2408-start-command-version-probe.mjs  # prints the installed `$` version and the in-place gate
```

On `main` (with only the two new modules copied in so that the imports resolve), 10 of the 12 tests fail. The two that pass are the tool-kill test, whose module comes from this PR, and the duplicate-report test, which was already fixed by #2397. The existing OOM and kill suites (#2134, #2301) were updated for the new default budget and pass.

## Unrelated CI fixes

`@sentry/node` and `@sentry/profiling-node` 11.3.0 and 11.4.0 were published on 2026-10-02 (12:56 and 16:37 UTC). After each release, the dependency-freshness gate failed on every branch, so the pins are refreshed to `^11.4.0`, following ef33600b. The #2187 pin test follows the new pins.

The Broken Link Checker failed on `main` (08:24 and 12:14 UTC) and on branches on 2026-10-02. Every error was a `503` from github.com, and every one was for one of the seven `github.com/.../blob/...` URLs that lychee checks here. These URLs answer 200 outside Actions. This branch first fixed it with a lychee `--remap` of blob URLs to `raw.githubusercontent.com` (a677ca60, Check Links green). `main` then merged #2423, which re-checks transient failures with backoff and checks blob pages through the contents API. After merging `main`, this PR drops the remap so only `main`’s mechanism remains, and it does not change the link workflow. The evidence and the remap, kept as a token-free alternative, are in `experiments/issue-2408-link-check-503/`.

## Remaining limits

- A recovered resource-limited session still has two log files when the installed `$` is older than 0.35.0.
- A genuine OOM recovery runs `solve --resume` as a new solve process, so solve's auto-restart counter starts again. The total is bounded by `--session-kill-resume-attempts` (default 3).
- A real cgroup OOM cannot be reproduced end to end in this sandbox (no memory cgroup controller); the tests replay real log tails and statuses.
- The in-process resume (RC5) works only when solve itself survives the OOM kill. Otherwise the bot-level recovery (RC1–RC4) handles it.
- The raw bot logs and the 46 MB solve log of `0760afb4` (from a private repository) were analysed but not committed. Only sanitized excerpts are in the case study.
